workarounds.symptom: `MCPServer` answers an unknown prompt name or a missing required argument with code `0` / `-32603`; the spec uses `-32602`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Return invalid params for unknown prompts and missing arguments. Target files: src/mcp/server/mcpserver/prompts/base.py, src/mcp/server/mcpserver/prompts/manager.py, src/mcp/server/mcpserver/server.py. Closes [#3669](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/issues/3669). (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3696)

workarounds.symptom: Client never retries after -32020 HeaderMismatch, and there is no public way to pre-load the x-mcp-header map (SEP-2243 client SHOULD/MAY both unimplemented)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Retry a tool call once after a HeaderMismatch rejection. Target files: src/mcp/client/client.py, tests/docs_src/test_header_parameters.py, tests/interaction/_requirements.py. On a 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP connection, `Client.call_tool` for a tool with `x-mcp-header` arguments failed with `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) unless that client had already listed the tool. It also kept failing when the tool's schema gained an annotation after it was listed. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3627)

workarounds.symptom: Server TokenHandler rejects the jwt-bearer (ID-JAG) grant from public CIMD clients, which the enterprise-managed authorization extension permits
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Describe the ID-JAG confidential-client rule as SDK policy, not a SEP-990 requirement. Target files: docs/client/identity-assertion.md, examples/snippets/clients/identity_assertion_client.py, examples/snippets/servers/identity_assertion_server.py. The SDK only lets confidential clients (ones with a shared secret) use the ID-JAG `jwt-bearer` grant, on both the client provider and the built-in authorization server. The docs, several comments and one error message said SEP-990 requires that. It doesn't, and this... (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3622)

workarounds.symptom: test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape fails on Windows without elevation or Developer Mode
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fall back to an NTFS junction when the symlink escape test can't create a symlink. Target files: tests/shared/test_path_security.py. `test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape` called `symlink_to()` unguarded. Windows only allows that for elevated processes or with Developer Mode on, so on an ordinary Windows dev machine the test errored with `WinError 1314` before it ever reached `safe_join`. CI didn't notice because the hosted Windows runners are allowed to create symlinks. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3609)
